Visit the official DU website: www.du.ac.in.
Click on "Jobs and Opportunities" under the head "Work with DU".
Read the qualification, experience, screening guidelines, and indicative proforma available on the website before filling the form.
Select the relevant advertisement (R&P/321/2026 for Associate Professor or R&P/322/2026 for Professor) and department.
Fill the online application form with complete and correct personal, educational, and experience information.

content_sections.heading: DU Associate Professor Vacancy 2026: Department-wise Details
content_sections.text: The 56 Associate Professor vacancies (Advt. No. R&P/321/2026) are distributed across departments as follows: Of the total 56 Associate Professor vacancies, 4 posts are reserved for PwBD (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities) candidates: 1 in Hindi (VI), and 2 in Philosophy (1-LD, 1-VI). PwBD reserved posts are open to candidates of any category - UR/SC/ST/OBC/EWS.

content_sections.heading: DU Professor Vacancy 2026: Department-wise Details
content_sections.text: The 30 Professor vacancies (Advt. No. R&P/322/2026) are distributed across departments as follows: Category abbreviations used: UR = Unreserved, SC = Scheduled Caste, ST = Scheduled Tribe, OBC = Other Backward Classes, EWS = Economically Weaker Sections, PwBD = Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (VI = Visual Impairment including blindness and low vision, LD = Locomotor Disability including leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims, and muscular dystrophy).

content_sections.heading: DU Associate Professor & Professor Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Eligibility requirements differ between the two posts, both requiring a PhD as a mandatory qualification, along with differing levels of teaching/research experience and research score. For the disciplines of Arts, Commerce, Humanities, Law, Social Sciences, Sciences, Languages, and Library Science, candidates must fulfil all of the following: A relaxation of 5% (from 55% to 50%) at the Bachelor's and Master's level is allowed for SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer)/PwBD (VI and LD categories) candidates, and for PhD degree holders who obtained their Master's degree prior to 19 September 1991. Only publications in the UGC-CARE list or SCOPUS-indexed journals are considered, subject to the UGC-CARE list's discontinuation cut-off of 11 February 2025. For the same set of disciplines, candidates must fulfil either of the following: Option A: An eminent scholar holding a PhD Degree in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline, actively engaged in research, with a minimum of 10 research publications in peer-reviewed or UGC-listed journals, and a total research score of 120 . Candidates must also have a minimum of ten years of teaching experience as Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor in a University/College, and/or equivalent research experience at University/National-level Institutions, with evidence of having successfully guided a doctoral candidate. Option B: An outstanding professional holding a PhD Degree in the relevant/allied/applied discipline from an academic institution (not covered under Option A) or industry, who has made a significant contribution to knowledge in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline, supported by documentary evidence, with ten years of experience. As with Associate Professor, only UGC-CARE list or SCOPUS-indexed publications are considered for research score, and the PhD Degree is a mandatory qualification for appointment to the post of Professor.

content_sections.heading: DU Associate Professor & Professor Salary
content_sections.text: Selected Associate Professors will be placed in Academic Pay Level-13A of the 7th Central Pay Commission Pay Matrix, and selected Professors will be placed in Academic Pay Level-14 , both carrying UGC pay scales plus admissible allowances. Discretionary advance increments may be awarded to candidates entering with higher merit, a high number of quality research publications, and relevant experience, at the discretion of the competent University authority based on Selection Committee recommendations.

content_sections.heading: DU Associate Professor & Professor Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for both posts follows a screening-and-interview process based on Academic/Research Score: The Screening Committee prepares a list of all candidates in descending order of research score. Candidates must meet the minimum required research score - 75 for Associate Professor, 120 for Professor - calculated based on research papers, publications, ICT/e-content contributions, research guidance, patents, policy documents, awards/fellowships, and invited lectures, as per the detailed scoring matrix in the Screening Guidelines. A minimum of 30 candidates for the first vacancy, and 10 candidates for every additional vacancy in each category, are called for interview, based on rank in the screening list. All candidates scoring equal to the cut-off for a category are also shortlisted. Shortlisted candidates are assessed through a presentation, graded A (Excellent), B (Good), C (Average), or D (Poor) by a Presentation Assessment Committee. This assessment is indicative only and not binding on the Selection Committee. The duly-constituted Selection Committee makes the final selection decision, which is final and binding. Mere fulfilment of the minimum qualification or eligibility criteria does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview. Publications "under submission" or submitted to referees are not considered for scoring, and research score is calculated only from a minimum of three out of six specified categories.

content_sections.heading: Required Documents
content_sections.text: Applicants seeking reservation benefits under SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer)/EWS/PwBD categories must upload the necessary category certificates in the Government-prescribed, digitally verifiable format, of the current financial year where applicable. PwBD candidates must have a disability of not less than 40% and must upload a valid Disability Certificate. Shortlisted candidates called for interview must bring original testimonials/certificates along with valid photo ID (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Driving License/Passport), plus self-attested photocopies of qualification, experience, and category documents. Candidates serving in Government/PSU/Autonomous Bodies must submit a No Objection Certificate (NOC) with vigilance clearance from their employer, either with the application or at the time of interview.

faq.question: Q1. What is DU Associate Professor & Professor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a pair of recruitment notifications by the University of Delhi (DU) for 56 Associate Professor posts (Advt. No. R&P/321/2026) and 30 Professor posts (Advt. No. R&P/322/2026) across nine departments — Chemistry, Environmental Studies, Genetics, Geology, Hindi, Linguistics, Operational Research, Philosophy, and Zoology.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in DU Associate Professor & Professor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 86 vacancies are available: 56 for Associate Professor and 30 for Professor, combined across nine departments.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for DU Associate Professor & Professor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date for receipt of application for both posts is 20 August 2026, or two weeks from the date of publication of the advertisement in the Employment News, whichever is later.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required for DU Associate Professor?
faq.answer: A PhD in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline, a Master's degree with at least 55% marks, a minimum of eight years of teaching/research experience, and a total research score of 75, along with a minimum of seven publications in peer-reviewed or UGC-listed journals.

faq.question: Q5. What is the qualification required for DU Professor?
faq.answer: Either an eminent scholar with a PhD, ten research publications, a total research score of 120, and ten years of teaching/research experience with successful doctoral guidance; or an outstanding professional with a PhD and ten years of relevant experience with documented contribution to the field.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for DU Associate Professor & Professor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: ₹2,000 for Unreserved candidates, ₹1,500 for OBC/EWS and women applicants, ₹1,000 for SC/ST, and ₹500 for PwBD candidates, for both posts.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for DU Associate Professor & Professor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates can apply online through www.du.ac.in under "Jobs and Opportunities" in the "Work with DU" section, submitting separate applications and fees for each post/department applied for.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for DU Associate Professor & Professor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Selection involves screening based on Academic/Research Score (minimum 75 for Associate Professor, 120 for Professor), shortlisting for interview, a presentation assessment, and final selection by a duly-constituted Selection Committee.
